issue.title: sync with socket.io 1.4.3 - support compression

repository.name: netty-socketio
repository.description: Socket.IO server implemented on Java. Realtime java framework

issue.body: Please could you add the compression support, introduced in the latest socket.io?

body: @mrniko I will need to re-check the rfc but are you sure it is valid to have both values in the "Connection:" header on an upgrade ?

socketio client runned in FireFox works by this way and socketio javascript server handles this correctly. It sends `Upgrade` value only in Chrome browser. Also websocket upgrade logic could be extracted to `protected` method for further extension.

I don't see anything preventing an `upgrade` co-existing with other options.

https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7230#section-6.7

> When Upgrade is sent, the sender MUST also send a Connection header
>    field (Section 6.1) that contains an "upgrade" connection option, in
>    order to prevent Upgrade from being accidentally forwarded by
>    intermediaries that might not implement the listed protocols.

Got it... Let me fix it

> Am 26.01.2016 um 18:37 schrieb Scott Mitchell notifications@github.com:
> 
> I don't see anything preventing an upgrade co-existing with other options.
> 
> https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7230#section-6.7
> 
> When Upgrade is sent, the sender MUST also send a Connection header
> field (Section 6.1) that contains an "upgrade" connection option, in
> order to prevent Upgrade from being accidentally forwarded by
> intermediaries that might not implement the listed protocols.
> 
> —
> Reply to this email directly or view it on GitHub.
Perhaps we should have a utility method to detect upgrade which uses [containsIgnoreCase](https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/4.1/common/src/main/java/io/netty/util/AsciiString.java#L1385)
